data.title: Undiluted launches to track the global venture debt and growth credit market
data.description:
Undiluted launches to track the global venture debt and growth credit market

Undiluted launches to track the global venture debt and growth credit market

PR Newswire

LONDON, Sept. 15, 2026

New specialist media & intelligence platform covers the lenders, deals and trends shaping growth debt globally

LONDON, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Undiluted, a new specialist media and intelligence platform focused on venture debt and growth credit, has officially launched.

The platform has been created to give investors, lenders, founders and advisers a clearer view of a market that has grown rapidly but remains fragmented and difficult to track.

Undiluted covers debt financing for technology and growth companies globally, including venture debt, growth credit and other forms of structured lending. Over time, the platform plans to expand beyond news and research into deeper data, benchmarking and market intelligence covering lenders, deals, pricing and activity.

Undiluted was founded by entrepreneur Alex Price, who previously founded and sold digital agency 93digital. His interest in the credit market developed partly through selling the business to a debt-financed group, giving him first-hand exposure to the role lenders and credit structures can play in the growth economy.

"The innovation economy has spent decades building better data, media and infrastructure around equity. Debt, particularly venture and growth debt, remains comparatively underserved despite becoming an increasingly important source of capital for ambitious companies," said Price.

"There are hundreds of lenders operating across the market with very different structures, terms and appetites. Deals are often inconsistently labelled, and founders can struggle to understand the options available to them."

Undiluted has launched with global news and deal coverage alongside resources for founders and finance leaders. Its planned offering includes structured deal data, benchmarking, proprietary research, a podcast and industry events.

The platform is also designed to reflect a growth lending market that increasingly extends beyond traditional venture debt.

"A growing number of companies are raising substantial debt facilities without having recently raised venture capital at all," Price added. "We want Undiluted to reflect how the market actually operates rather than forcing every transaction into traditional asset class categories."

Undiluted is headquartered in London and covers the growth debt market globally.

For more information, visit undiluted.com.

About Undiluted

Undiluted is a specialist media and intelligence platform tracking the global venture debt and growth credit market. It provides news, research and insights on the companies, transactions, lenders and trends shaping growth lending globally, with deeper data and intelligence products in development.

data.title: Meet UROVO UPad: The Flagship Commercial Tablet for Connected Frontline Operations
data.description:
Meet UROVO UPad: The Flagship Commercial Tablet for Connected Frontline Operations

Meet UROVO UPad: The Flagship Commercial Tablet for Connected Frontline Operations

PR Newswire

SINGAPORE, Sept. 15, 2026

One intelligent platform integrating payment, barcode scanning, RFID, and enterprise mobility

SINGAPORE, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- UROVO today introduced UPad, its flagship commercial tablet designed to simplify frontline operations by integrating payment, professional barcode scanning, RFID, and enterprise mobility into a single intelligent platform. By replacing multiple disconnected devices, UPad helps businesses streamline workflows, improve productivity, and gain real-time operational visibility.

"Frontline operations today require more than standalone devices," said Zhang Bo, CTO of UROVO. "UPad brings together payment, data capture, mobility, and business applications in one platform, helping organizations operate more efficiently and deliver better customer experiences."

Built on UROVO's innovative Quick Lock modular architecture, UPad quickly adapts between handheld, countertop, and wall-mounted configurations, allowing a single device to support multiple operational scenarios while reducing hardware investment and simplifying deployment.

UPad is designed for a wide range of industries, including retail for assisted selling, inventory management, and mobile checkout; restaurants for ordering and tableside payment; hospitality for guest services and mobile staff operations; and warehousing and logistics for inventory control and asset tracking.

Powered by a Qualcomm octa-core processor built on an advanced 4 nm process, UPad delivers responsive performance with excellent power efficiency. It features Wi-Fi 6E, optional Wi-Fi HaLow, an 8,000 mAh removable battery, and an 11-inch display that supports glove and wet-touch operation, ensuring reliable performance throughout demanding workdays.

UPad also integrates enterprise technologies into one device, including SoftPOS payments with NFC Tap-to-Pay support, professional barcode scanning, and optional UHF RFID powered by the Impinj E-series chipset with GEN2X support for fast inventory tracking and real-time asset visibility.

Fully integrated with UROVO UMS (Unified Management System), UPad enables IT teams to remotely deploy, configure, monitor, and manage devices from a centralized platform, simplifying large-scale deployments while reducing maintenance costs.

By combining mobility, payment, barcode scanning, RFID, and centralized device management into a unified platform, UPad helps organizations improve operational efficiency, reduce device complexity, and accelerate digital transformation.

Learn more at https://en.urovo.com/.

data.title: The Fed may be on the verge of a serious mistake, prominent economists warn
data.description:
By Greg Robb

Some economists are calling on the central bank to wait before raising interest rates, out of concern the economy may be vulnerable beneath the surface

Traders see a 92% chance that the Federal Reserve, led by Kevin Warsh, will increase interest rates at its meeting this week.

Investors on Wall Street and observers of the Federal Reserve in Washington largely expect the central bank to raise interest rates when it meets this week, but some prominent economists are warning that such a move could prove to be a mistake.

They see the economy as more vulnerable to a steep slowdown in growth than commonly believed. The Fed's job is to keep employment steady and inflation under control. If central bank officials raise rates on Wednesday, the goal will be to cool inflation. But these economists worry that a rate hike could cause a sharp cut in economic activity, which could prompt businesses to let go of workers and ultimately lead to a recession.

"The odds of a serious Fed policy mistake are uncomfortably high and rising," warned Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody's Analytics, in a post on X.

It's hard to slow economic growth without layoffs, rising unemployment and igniting a "self-reinforcing negative cycle," said Zandi, who has advised leading Democrats over the years.

In late August, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh used his remarks at the Jackson Hole economic symposium to signal that he was concerned about inflation trends. He said he wouldn't hesitate to act if the inflation picture worsened.

Ten days ago, investors put the odds of a rate hike at about 50%. But rising diesel prices, renewed tensions in the Middle East and Friday's hotter-than-expected consumer inflation report have convinced traders and economists that Warsh will follow through on his tough talk and raise rates.

Fed officials will meet behind closed doors Tuesday and Wednesday to decide whether to hike interest rates or hold them steady. The Fed's decision will be announced at 2 p.m. Eastern time on Wednesday, and Warsh will hold a press conference at 2:30 p.m.

Carl Tannenbaum, chief economist at Northern Trust, said the argument for raising rates isn't as clear-cut as the markets and many commentators believe, adding that the central bank has no easy options.

While economic activity has remained buoyant in the face of the war and tariffs, he said, "the economy is not invulnerable."

Lower-income households are tapping into savings to keep up with inflation, he noted.

"Holding rates steady would provide additional time to assess whether there are potential cracks in the foundation of the expansion," Tannenbaum said in an email to clients.

Steve Englander, global head of G10 FX Research at Standard Chartered, said a hike would be premature given the crosscurrents in the inflation data.

He said the correct Fed policy decision would be to stay on hold until these contradictory signals abate.

For the Fed to raise rates and then have to reverse course and cut rates in a few months would be seen as Warsh having "a very unsteady hand on the tiller."

Some economists think the markets have gone too far in pricing in a hike.

Michael Strain, director of economic policy studies at the American Enterprise Institute, said that the market is reading the Fed wrong and that the "center of gravity" among Fed officials still supports keeping rates unchanged.

Without higher energy prices and tariffs, underlying inflation would be closer to 2.5%, not far above the Fed's 2% target, he said.

Although the likelihood of a rate increase has certainly gone up in recent weeks, Michael Pearce, chief U.S. economist at Oxford Economics, said the September decision could still go either way.

"We're sticking with our forecast that the Fed leaves rate on hold," Pearce said in a note to clients.

-Greg Robb

data.title: SES and Elveo Mobile Deepen Collaboration to Advance Direct-to-Device Services in Europe
data.description:
SES and Elveo Mobile Deepen Collaboration to Advance Direct-to-Device Services in Europe

SES, a global leader in space solutions, and Elveo Mobile, the company that delivers mobile connectivity and elevated intelligence for a planet on the move, today announced the expansion of their collaboration to accelerate delivery of direct-to-device (D2D) services in Europe.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260915183604/en/

SES and Elveo Mobile Deepen Collaboration to Advance Direct-to-Device Services in Europe

SES will leverage Elveo’s patented, proven and cost-effective D2D technology to enable seamless mobile roaming capabilities for European consumers, businesses, governments, institutional, and defense users.

To further this vision, SES and Elveo Mobile will collaborate to establish manufacturing capabilities and a robust supply chain in Europe for the productions of the Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) D2D satellites, using Elveo’s patented D2D satellite bus, payload and software technology stack.

These LEO D2D satellites will form part of a unique multi-orbit architecture, combining Elveo’s LEO D2D network with SES’s geostationary (GEO) and Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) networks capable of delivering secure and reliable connectivity to European governments and institutions, including NATO.

European customers also stand to benefit from SES’s global distribution of Elveo’s D2D services, which use Elveo’s high-priority 2 GHz S-band spectrum rights and a global market access footprint currently covering more than one billion people.

"European consumers, commercial, and government users deserve resilient, secure, multi-orbit connectivity, and SES is preparing to deliver that next layer of communications in combination with Elveo’s direct-to-device services," said Adel Al-Saleh, Chief Executive Officer, SES. "Working with our partner Elveo will help bring critical D2D services to European customers on the timeline they demand."

"SES is the right partner for Elveo to bring D2D services to Europe," said Ramu Potarazu, CEO of Elveo. "Together, we are committed to delivering D2D connectivity for European customers and establishing the manufacturing capabilities needed to support them. By working closely with SES, we are confident we can accelerate access to critical D2D connectivity for European mobile operators and governments that depend on them.”

About SES

At SES, we believe that space has the power to make a difference. That's why we design space solutions that help governments protect, businesses grow, and people stay connected—no matter where they are. With integrated multi-orbit satellites and our global terrestrial network, we deliver resilient, seamless connectivity and the highest quality video content to those shaping what's next. Following our Intelsat acquisition, we now offer more than 100 years of combined global industry leadership—backed by a track record of bringing innovation "firsts" to market. As a trusted partner to customers and the global space ecosystem, SES is driving impact that goes far beyond coverage. The company is headquartered in Luxembourg and listed on Paris and Luxembourg stock exchanges (Ticker: SESG). Further information is available at: www.ses.com.

About Elveo

Elveo is the premiere non-terrestrial mobile connectivity company, delivering elevated intelligence for a planet on the move. Elveo offers reliable, next-generation connectivity directly from satellites to smartphones, IoT devices and machines worldwide. Elveo is a globally inclusive company that offers mobile network operators and partners a resilient, always-on next-generation network to connect their customers across enterprise, government and humanitarian sectors.

For more information, visit elveo.com.

data.title: Scania G-series and R-series achieve five-star Euro NCAP results
data.description:
Scania G-series and R-series achieve five-star Euro NCAP results

Scania G-series and R-series achieve five-star Euro NCAP results

PR Newswire

SÖDERTÄLJE, Sweden, Sept. 15, 2026

SÖDERTÄLJE, Sweden, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Scania's G-series and R-series have been awarded five stars in Euro NCAP's haulage assessment, with a 96 percent score for crash avoidance. The results reflect Scania's continued focus on visibility, driver support, and advanced driver assistance systems in long-haulage and regional transport operations.

The Euro NCAP Haulage assessment covers:

  • Scania R-series 4x2 tractor
  • Scania R-series 6x2 rigid
  • Scania G-series 4x2 tractor
  • Scania G-series 6x2 rigid

Scania's G-series and R-series are made for different long-haulage and regional transport needs but share the same safety approach: supporting the driver through good direct vision, comfort, control, and advanced driver assistance systems.

Euro NCAP's haulage sector focuses on heavy vehicles in long-haul and highway-oriented operations. To enhance safety in these environments, Scania's R- and G series have SSCC (Speed Sign Cruise Control) and CSCC (Curve speed Cruise Control), adding safety in the driver support systems, especially in combination with SSA (Safe Stop Assist). The AEB (Autonomous Emergency Braking) and the VRUBS (Vulnerable Road User Brake System) strongly contribute to the score of 96 percent for the trucks in Crash Avoidance.

"Safety in long-haulage starts with supporting the driver. Visibility, comfort, driver assistance, and vehicle control all contribute to safer operations. The G-series and R-series show how Scania adapts these strengths to different transport assignments, while keeping the driver environment familiar," says Lars Gustafsson, Head of Trucks, Scania.

Euro NCAP highlighted the R-series for its solid performance in Safe Driving and Collision Avoidance, including optional camera monitor systems that improve front corner vision and reduce driver workload. It also noted the R-series' broad range of crash avoidance technologies, including AEB (Autonomous Emergency Braking) performance that supports avoidance of collisions with other vehicles, including those with only two wheels, as well as people.

The G-series was recognised for its balanced safety performance. Euro NCAP described it as a safe all-rounder when specified with the appropriate safety equipment. Its lower cab, deep windows and low belt line support direct vision in mixed transport environments.

Euro NCAP also gave the City Safe Award to both the G- and R-series. This adds to the five-star results already achieved by Scania's L- and P-series, showing how the modular system can support strong safety performance across the cab range.

"Since the introduction of Euro NCAP's Safer Truck programme, Scania has consistently pushed safety forward cross-sector in the transport sector and is continuing to encourage customers to buy the safest options and technologies available. We look forward to working with Scania on safety development way into the future," says Matthew Avery, Director for Strategic Development, Euro NCAP.

The G- and R-series are integrated within Scania's modular system. This means that drivers recognise the layout, controls, and working environment across the Scania range, supporting familiarity, efficiency, and comfort in daily operations. For customers, vehicles can be specified for the right assignment, with the safety systems and cab configuration that best match the operation.

"Euro NCAP's assessment reflects the increasing expectations placed on heavy vehicles by customers, transport buyers, cities, and society. Safe trucks are essential for everyone who shares the road. We provide vehicles and systems that support the driver, reduce risk, and help customers operate safely and efficiently," says Gustafsson.

The result underlines Scania's focus on safety across the applications where the G-series and R-series are used. For customers, the benefit is a familiar driver environment, matched with safety systems and cab specifications that suit the assignment.

Explore Scania's five-star Euro NCAP results and discover the safety features across our truck range here.

data.title: HawkEye 360 Establishes First European Subsidiary in Luxembourg
data.description:
HawkEye 360 Establishes First European Subsidiary in Luxembourg

HawkEye 360 Establishes First European Subsidiary in Luxembourg

PR Newswire

PARIS, Sept. 15, 2026

New EU entity reinforces HawkEye 360's long-term commitment to European customers, allies and industry partners

PARIS, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- HawkEye 360, Inc. (NYSE: HAWK), today announced the establishment of its first European subsidiary, HawkEye 360 Luxembourg, S.à r.l., marking an important step in the Company's expansion of operations in the European Union and reinforcing its long-term commitment to European customers, allies and industry partners amid an increasingly complex security environment.

The announcement coincides with an engagement between HawkEye 360 Chief Executive Officer John Serafini and U.S. Ambassador to Luxembourg Stacey Feinberg during World Space Business Week in Paris. The meeting underscores HawkEye 360's commitment to building a stronger operational presence in Europe and deepening its partnerships with government, industry and space-sector organizations across the region.

"Europe, its allies and our partners across the region are central to HawkEye 360's long-term strategy," said John Serafini, Chief Executive Officer of HawkEye 360. "The security environment is changing rapidly, and European nations need proven capabilities that can contribute to missions today. Establishing a European entity in Luxembourg strengthens our ability to work alongside governments and industry, support sovereign national requirements, and bring our proven space-based RF capabilities closer to the customers and partners who need them."

The Luxembourg subsidiary will serve as the foundation for HawkEye 360's expanded operations in the European Union, supporting closer engagement with European customers, governments and industry partners. The new entity provides a local base from which HawkEye 360 can build deeper relationships across Europe's defense and space ecosystem and collaborate more directly with European partners pursuing major emerging defense programs.

Operating an EU-based entity positions HawkEye 360 to participate more directly in Europe's evolving defense and space industrial ecosystem. By working from within the region, the Company is better positioned to collaborate with sovereign partners, work alongside European industry, and support solutions designed around European mission and security requirements.

"Luxembourg has built a strong and forward-looking space and defense ecosystem, making it an excellent partner for U.S. companies committed to supporting Europe's security, resilience and technological leadership," said Stacey Feinberg, U.S. Ambassador to Luxembourg. "HawkEye 360's decision to establish its European hub here reflects the strength of Luxembourg's growing space sector and creates new opportunities for collaboration."

HawkEye 360 provides proven space-based RF data and analytics that help defense and national security organizations detect, characterize, and understand activity across the radio frequency spectrum. As European nations strengthen their defense capabilities in response to evolving security challenges, HawkEye 360 can provide an operationally relevant RF layer that complements sovereign and allied systems, delivering unclassified, shareable insights to support situational awareness and informed decision-making.

"Our commitment to Europe starts with being closer to the customers and partners we support," said Todd Probert, Chief Operating Officer of HawkEye 360. "Europe's defense requirements are accelerating, and customers need capabilities that can be integrated and operationalized quickly. A European entity gives us a stronger foundation to collaborate directly with European industry, respond to major emerging defense programs, and integrate our proven RF capabilities with sovereign technologies and solutions developed within the region."

PHOTO CAPTION
HawkEye 360 Chief Executive Officer John Serafini meets with U.S. Ambassador to Luxembourg Stacey Feinberg during World Space Business Week in Paris as HawkEye 360 announces plans to establish its first European subsidiary in Luxembourg and expand its operations in the European Union. (L to R: Nuno Vilaca, SVP/General Manager, International, HawkEye 360; John Serafini, CEO, HawkEye 360; Ambassador Stacey Feinberg, Luxembourg; Alex Fox, President, HawkEye 360 International; Craig Searle, CFO, HawkEye 360; and Patrick Zeitouni, Chief Strategy Officer, HawkEye 360)

About HawkEye 360

HawkEye 360 is equipping defense, intelligence, and national security leaders with mission-critical electronic warfare to enable faster, better decision-making. By detecting, geolocating, and characterizing radio-frequency emissions worldwide, HawkEye 360 delivers trusted domain awareness and early-warning indicators to the US Government and allied partners. Our space-based collection, proprietary signal processing, and AI-powered analytics transform knowledge of RF spectrum into a strategic advantage. Proven by operational mission success, HawkEye 360 is redefining how signals intelligence strengthens national and global security.

data.title: Scottish Rite for Children Honored Again as No. 1 in the Nation for Pediatric Orthopedic Care by U.S. News & World Report
data.description:
Scottish Rite for Children Honored Again as No. 1 in the Nation for Pediatric Orthopedic Care by U.S. News & World Report

Scottish Rite for Children Honored Again as No. 1 in the Nation for Pediatric Orthopedic Care by U.S. News & World Report

PR Newswire

DALLAS, Sept. 15, 2026

Institution earns top ranking for a second consecutive year, reflecting its longstanding
commitment to patient care and giving children back their childhood

DALLAS, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- U.S. News & World Report ranked Scottish Rite for Children No. 1 in the nation for pediatric orthopedic care in its 2026-2027 Best Children's Hospitals specialty rankings.

For nearly two decades, Scottish Rite has placed among the nation's top pediatric orthopedic programs in collaboration with Children's Medical Center Dallas and UT Southwestern Medical Center. This marks the first time the organization has earned the No. 1 ranking in consecutive years.

"We are deeply honored by this recognition because it represents the exceptional care we provide to children and families every day," said Robert L. Walker, president and CEO of Scottish Rite for Children. "Our greatest measure of success will always be the difference we make in their lives. This honor belongs to the people across Scottish Rite who make that possible."

U.S. News develops its annual rankings in partnership with RTI International, which collected and analyzed data from 114 children's hospitals and surveyed thousands of pediatric specialists. The rankings consider factors including clinical outcomes, compliance with established best practices and level and quality of hospital resources directly related to patient care.

"This recognition reflects Scottish Rite's continued work to advance pediatric orthopedic care," said Daniel J. Sucato, M.D., M.S., chief of staff at Scottish Rite for Children. "Every advancement we make starts with a simple question: How can we provide better care for this child?"

This year, Scottish Rite performed the first U.S. implantation of a newly FDA-cleared device to treat early-onset scoliosis, expanding treatment options for children with complex spinal conditions.

In recent years, the National Institutes of Health awarded Scottish Rite R01 grants totaling $4.1 million to advance research for osteonecrosis.

Scottish Rite also advances the field through education. The Dorothy & Bryant Edwards Fellowship in Pediatric Orthopedics and Scoliosis, the largest pediatric orthopedic fellowship in the world, graduated its 200th fellow this year.

"Our strength comes from the way clinical care, research and education work together at Scottish Rite," Sucato said. "That approach allows us to advance pediatric orthopedics and, most importantly, provide the best possible care for every child."

About Scottish Rite for Children 
Scottish Rite for Children has been dedicated to giving children back their childhood for more than a century. The institution is a world-renowned leader in the treatment of pediatric orthopedic conditions, such as scoliosis, clubfoot, hand differences, hip disorders, limb lengthening and reconstruction, sports injuries and fractures, as well as certain related arthritic and neurological disorders and learning disorders, such as dyslexia. The organization conducts innovative research and provides high-level education opportunities for medical professionals around the world. Scottish Rite operates two campuses, including a hospital in Dallas, Texas, and an ambulatory surgery center in Frisco, Texas, and is known for being a bright, child-friendly place that does not look or feel like a health care institution. Patients receive treatment regardless of their family's ability to pay. For more information about services available at the Dallas or Frisco campuses, volunteering or donating, visit scottishriteforchildren.org.
